The reviewer-fix pass added the /Items/Root structural note above and closed the stored-kind regressions the PlaylistsFolder switch had orphaned (CanDelete, ICollectionFolder classification, the playlists-library browse).  2026-08-30 batch C2 reviewer-fix pass: the Apply row's `body-diff`/deep_verified verdict was WITHDRAWN - it had been won inside a seconds-wide window while the suite's own library scan was in flight, and the two servers do not hold the same item once that scan lands. The journey now forces the scan and waits for it, the row is red on `unlocked_after_scan`, and the scan-overwrites-Identify divergence is recorded on its own row with the C# citation and the un-defer path. The same pass demoted that row's method from `body-diff` to `property` (it compares a named projection of the read-back, not a body), paired every fetcher-gate assertion in reads.py with a positive control so a musicbrainz.org 503 can no longer satisfy one, stopped a Ferrofin 5xx being laundered into a dropped leg, and fixed the `RefreshLibrary` scheduled task to await its scan (it reported itself finished in 0 ms with the scan still writing, where v10.11.8 `RefreshMediaLibraryTask.ExecuteAsync` awaits `ValidateMediaLibraryInternal`). Half of that port is worse than none of it: reading the stamps without gating on them costs a query per scan and changes nothing, and the stamp alone moves `Etag` and the `minDateLastSaved` filter on every DTO in the API without the perf run that change is owed. Two consequences beyond the row that exposed it, both corrections of the same defect: the six `requires-livetv-tuner`, two `requires-channel-plugin` and two `remote-opt-in` rows record a MISSING PROBE, not a divergence, and now render under "No probe yet (NOT accepted, NOT verified)" instead of being counted as settled decisions; and the `verified`/`verified-by-push-probe` rows render as notes rather than as accepted divergences. No row's TEXT was rewritten to move it — only the bucket its declared category was already claiming.  2026-08-30 batch F6 (the last accepted divergences and opt-in probes, re-examined from the C# rather than trusted): four of the six rows in this batch had the WRONG CATEGORY and two described the wrong operation. `POST /Startup/User` was `accepted-divergence` on the grounds that Ferrofin ports "the Forbid guard upstream added in v12" — under the campaign's master-vs-10.11.8 rule that is outcome 1, not a divergence: the guard is upstream security commit 62a5ded920, Ferrofin ports both of its halves, and it is now `jellyfin-bug`. DELETE /LiveTv/TunerHosts.classification: accepted-divergence, SIDE EFFECT ONLY (the verdict on this row is the configuration read-back, not this): `LiveTvController.DeleteTunerHost` (Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/LiveTvController.cs:1000-1006 @ v10.11.8) rewrites `LiveTvOptions.TunerHosts`, saves, and returns — it queues NO `RefreshGuideScheduledTask`, unlike `ListingsManager.DeleteListingsProvider` (src/Jellyfin.LiveTv/Listings/ListingsManager.cs:83-91) which does. Measured on the loop pair 2026-08-30, both servers taking a case-flipped id and answering 204: immediately after the DELETE F reports 0 channels AND 0 programmes (the airings are FK children of the channel rows, so they go too) where it had 2 / 19200, while J still reports 2 / 338. Both servers converge on the SAME end state — Jellyfin's next refresh deletes exactly those rows, because `GuideManager.CleanDatabase` (src/Jellyfin.LiveTv/Guide/GuideManager.cs:147-148, 331-360 @ v10.11.8) removes every `LiveTvChannel`/`LiveTvProgram` the pass did not re-emit, and a channel of a tuner that no longer exists is never re-emitted — and what differs is the window in between, during which Jellyfin serves channels no tuner can stream. Ferrofin keeps the cascade (see the 'don't port Jellyfin bugs' rule): a dangling channel is a 5xx waiting for a client that tries to play it. NOT PORTED, deliberately, and NOT hidden: the journey asserts this op on the configuration, which is what both servers agree the delete means, and this note is the record of what it does not assert.

DELETE /Playlists/{playlistId}/Users/{us.classification: jellyfin-bug: Jellyfin's DELETE is a silent no-op on BOTH v10.11.8 and master. `PlaylistsController.RemoveUserFromPlaylist` (identical in both trees) resolves the share from one Playlist instance, then `PlaylistManager.RemoveUserFromShares` (v10.11.8 L641-648 / master L669-676, byte-identical) re-fetches a DIFFERENT instance via GetPlaylistForUser -> GetPlaylists -> LibraryManager.GetItemList (master L1656-1673, which returns _itemRepository.GetItemList directly, bypassing the BaseItem cache and materialising fresh objects) and calls `shares.Remove(share)`. `MediaBrowser.Model/Entities/PlaylistUserPermissions.cs:8` is a plain class with only UserId/CanEdit auto-properties — no Equals, no IEquatable, not a record — so `EqualityComparer<T>.Default` is REFERENCE equality, Remove returns false, the UNCHANGED list is written back, and the controller returns 204. Corroborated inside the same file: `AddUserToShares` removes an element it took from the SAME list, which is why POST works and DELETE does not. `git log v10.11.8..master` over both paths contains no change to RemoveUserFromShares — MASTER HAS NOT FIXED THIS. Ferrofin deletes by (playlist_id, user_id) in SQL (ferrofin-core/src/collection_manager.rs `remove_user_from_shares`), which is the semantic intent of the C#, so the share actually goes and a repeat DELETE correctly 404s — the controller's own `share is null -> NotFound("User permissions not found")` branch, which on Jellyfin is unreachable. Ferrofin is the correct side. Measured on the F6 pair 2026-08-30, twice: F 204 then GET Users [] then repeat DELETE 404; J 204 then GET Users STILL lists the user then repeat DELETE 204. Discriminating control on the SAME Jellyfin instance: `POST /Playlists/{id}` with `Users: []` (UpdatePlaylist assigns the list wholesale, no List.Remove) DOES clear and persist — so this is not container skew, fixture or a Shares-persistence problem, it is RemoveUserFromShares alone. Previously filed `instance` (instance noise / methodology), which was wrong: a deterministic, twice-reproduced upstream defect is not lab noise. The row cannot reach deep_verified while upstream is broken — journeys.py requires the write's effect on BOTH servers and Jellyfin's legitimately does not hold. That is the correct terminal state for a jellyfin-bug row, not a probe weakness. The second symptom is now recorded rather than asserted: `j_playlist_share` reports the repeat-DELETE status under `notes.playlist_share_repeat_delete_status` in journey-results.json (measured F=404 J=204, twice), deliberately kept OUT of the row's boolean so a future Ferrofin regression to a blind 204 cannot pass by matching Jellyfin.

The previous note said 'a compiled-in extension honestly rejects with 400 where Jellyfin can uninstall any plugin'. DELETE /ScheduledTasks/Running/{taskId}.classification: jellyfin-bug: stopping a task that is no longer running is 500 on Jellyfin and 204 on Ferrofin. `ScheduledTaskWorker.Cancel()` (v10.11.8:377-385) opens with `if (State != TaskState.Running) throw new InvalidOperationException("Cannot cancel a Task unless it is in the Running state.")`, and `ScheduledTasksController.StopTask` calls `_taskManager.Cancel(task)` with no catch, so the exception reaches the error middleware. The action declares only 204 and 404 (`[ProducesResponseType(Status204NoContent)]`, `Status404NotFound`) and the vendored contract declares no 500 for this path, so the throw is unintended, not a documented behaviour — Ferrofin's `FerrofinTaskManager::stop_run` returns Ok for an already-idle task (404 only for an unknown id) and is kept correct (do not port Jellyfin bugs). MEASURED 2026-08-30 on the loop pair, deterministic, not a race: POST-then-DELETE on `ec2f221fd8e7706b3d3afd2c4591b4d7` (Audio Normalization) is (204, 500) four times running on Jellyfin and (204, 204) four times on Ferrofin, and a DELETE with nothing running at all is 500 vs 204. The journeys row therefore reads H=True J=False and only goes red on a WARM lab: the first Audio Normalization run does real work and is still Running when the DELETE lands (which is why an earlier journeys record has it green), while every later run finishes in well under a millisecond. Ferrofin's own leg passes on both.

GET /Albums/{itemId}/Similar.classification: flat-provider methodology (SET-GATED, order not gateable). Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). Ferrofin runs the same query and, as of this pass, the same `Random` order. IT BRIEFLY DID NOT: batch A2 first shipped `SortName` here, which is not cosmetic — at limit < |candidates| a fixed order returns a DIFFERENT ITEM, measured on the loop pair as `/Items/{audio}/Similar?limit=1` answering 'Artist 01 Album 01 Track 02' on five consecutive Ferrofin calls while Jellyfin alternated Track 02 / Track 03. That divergence is now closed in the server (`similar_items_manager.rs::flat_similar`, unit test `the_flat_provider_orders_random_not_by_name`), not papered over. WHAT THIS LEDGER ROW DOES AND DOES NOT GATE: `Random` on both sides means the ORDER can never be diffed by any probe, and neither can a page narrower than the candidate pool — parity_diff aligns arrays by Path>Name>Id, so a reordered Items array returns 0 diffs and always will. The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GREEN BUT VACUOUS ON THE CURRENT FIXTURE — read this row as 'no divergence detected', not as 'verified'. `suite/perf/gen-fixtures.sh` gave each of the 3 albums a UNIQUE music genre, so the candidate universe is empty by construction on BOTH servers and the leg diffs `{"Items": [], "TotalRecordCount": 0}` against itself. The fixture is changed (two of the three artists now share a genre) but that only takes effect at the campaign's final wipe-and-provision; until that sweep runs, the album matching itself is covered by the `an_album_seed_matches_albums_sharing_a_genre_only` unit test (two albums sharing a genre, a same-genre track that must NOT come back because IncludeItemTypes is [MusicAlbum] alone, and the ExcludeArtistIds leg with a positive control). A real Ferrofin bug found behind this row IS fixed and verified live: album Genres/Studios/PremiereDate are inherited from the album's Audio children (C# AlbumMetadataService + MetadataService.UpdateGenres/UpdateStudios/UpdatePremiereDate); Ferrofin aggregated only album-artist and year, so every album had `Genres: []` and was unreachable by the Genres= query this endpoint issues. After the fix, F album Genres/PremiereDate/ProductionYear match J exactly (Jazz/Rock/Ambient, 2022-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z, 2022).

GET /Artists/{itemId}/Similar.classification: open-work (NOT accepted): Ferrofin returns 0 rows where Jellyfin returns 2. The scorer half is fixed — the seed's kind now selects the C# provider shape (`MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider` is a flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [MusicArtist] }`, and an EMPTY Genres/Tags pair is not a predicate, so an untagged artist must match every other artist; covered by the `an_untagged_artist_seed_still_matches_every_other_artist` unit test). What still blocks it is the item-UNIVERSE divergence, not the similarity code: Ferrofin materializes MusicArtist as a parentless by-name row with a NULL TopParentId, and every user-scoped `InternalItemsQuery` is scoped to the user's views via `TopParentId IS NOT NULL` (item_repository.rs `scope_to_user_libraries`, the port of C# `AddUserToQuery`), so no artist is reachable by any query that does not name it by id. Detector, both servers: `/Items?userId=<u>&recursive=true&includeItemTypes=MusicArtist` -> F 0, J 3, while `/Artists?userId=<u>` returns all 3 on both, and adding `&ids=<artistId>` makes the same query return the row on Ferrofin. Same root cause as the MusicArtist/Folder/TvChannel/UserView rows missing from GET /Items/Suggestions. Un-defer path: give the MusicArtist by-name row a TopParentId (Jellyfin's artist rows are physical folder items under the music library, which is why they survive `AddUserToQuery`) — this changes the recursive item universe server-wide, so it needs its own change with the perf gate, not a ride-along. ORDERING, for the record: this endpoint's provider orders `Random` on both servers (MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50 / v10.11.8 LibraryController.cs:801) and Ferrofin now emits `Random` too, so when the universe bug is fixed the reads leg must stay pinned at a limit above the candidate pool — the ORDER is not gateable by any probe, since parity_diff aligns arrays by key.

Ferrofin compiles LrcLib in the way it compiles TMDB in. GET /Audio/{itemId}/universal.classification: security-fixed 2026-08-30 (batch S1, cross-user authz): C# RequestHelpers.GetUserId (v10.11.8 Jellyfin.Api/Helpers/RequestHelpers.cs:67-85) has two halves: an absent/all-zero userId falls back to the caller, and a userId that is NOT the caller is honoured only for an ADMINISTRATOR, else SecurityException -> 403. Ferrofin ported only the first half here. Found by the S1 sweep. The handler took no userId at all; it is the audio playback path (v10.11.8 UniversalAudioController.cs:120). Measured on the fixture: the file is 775053 B / 1.023 s = 6,060,832 bps, so Jellyfin's MediaSources[].Bitrate of 6,253,020 exceeds what the file physically contains, while Ferrofin's 6,061,020 matches ffprobe's own format.bit_rate. Upstream fixed this itself in PR #16248 (master PRN.cs:979-991 comments that formatInfo.BitRate is the container, not the video bitrate) and Ferrofin ports the fixed form. (2) PROBE-DTO NULLABILITY (Level / IsAVC / Width / Height). Upstream MASTER declares all four nullable — MediaBrowser.MediaEncoding/Probing/MediaStreamInfo.cs:93 `public int? Width`, :107 `public int? Height`, :170 `public int? Level`, :233 `public bool? IsAvc` — so a stream for which ffprobe emits no such key keeps null. v10.11.8 declares the same four as non-nullable value types at the same file's :95 `public int Width`, :109 `public int Height`, :172 `public int Level`, :235 `public bool IsAvc`, so an absent key deserializes to the CLR default and 10.11.8 then emits `Level: 0` and `IsAVC: false` on EVERY stream — audio and subtitle included, where neither value is meaningful — plus `Width: 0`/`Height: 0` on a text subtitle. GET /Packages/{name}.classification: property-verified: the two catalogues are each server's own repository content, so the single-package BODY is not comparable across instances, but every branch of InstallationManager.FilterPackages is. reads.py's `packages_by_name_invariants` derives 17 facts from each server's OWN /Packages[0] and diffs the fact dicts (a fact that is False on Ferrofin fails the row even when Jellyfin agrees): exact + case-insensitive name, guid-beats-name (`if (!id.IsEmpty()) ... else if (name is not null) ...` — the two predicates are alternatives, guid wins), an empty and an all-zeros guid falling through to the name (`IsEmpty()`), an unknown name as 404, the single-package body equalling that catalogue entry, and the WHOLE `Guid?` model-binding format set. THE FORMAT SET WAS THE HOLE, and it was a real live divergence, not a documentation slip: the fact list enumerated N, D and B and stopped, while `uuid::Uuid::parse_str` — what the handler used — is NOT `Guid.TryParse`'s set. Measured on the loop pair 2026-08-30, before the fix: `(guid)` (P) was 400 on Ferrofin and 200 on Jellyfin; `{0x...,{0x..}}` (X) was 400 and 200; a value padded with whitespace was 400 and 200 (.NET trims both ends); and `urn:uuid:guid`, which .NET refuses and `parse_str` accepts, was 200 and 400. Fixed in Rust, not in the probe: ferrofin_util::guid_extensions::parse_dotnet_guid ports Guid.TryParseGuid's dispatch (trim, then '(' -> ExactP, '{' -> ExactB when it contains a hyphen else ExactX, otherwise ExactD/ExactN) including TryParseExactX's two documented compat quirks — it eats whitespace anywhere, and its components are read as 32-bit so `0x1031b` is an accepted spelling of the short component `0x031b`, while a byte component above 0xFF is rejected. Both guid-bound plugin routes (GET /Packages/{name} and POST /Packages/Installed/{name}) bind through it. Re-measured after the fix: 27 spellings, all agreeing — the 12 basic ones and 15 exotic X/whitespace/overflow cases (truncating short-component overflow, 9-significant-digit overflow, a doubled 0x prefix, a missing 0x prefix, an empty component, 7 and 9 byte components, trailing junk, a leading '+', interior whitespace in D and P). NOT FIXED, recorded: the same `Uuid::parse_str` narrowness remains on every OTHER guid-bound route (axum's `Path<Uuid>`/`Query` extractors and handlers::query_parse), so P and X spellings are still refused there and `urn:uuid:` still accepted; no client sends either, and widening it is a whole-surface change this batch did not measure. Superseded the Layer-1 row, whose {name} was filled from a GENRE (sweep.py resolve_fixtures) so the live probe was GET /Packages/Action — 404/404 with the lookup never issued.

WHAT THE PROBE ISSUES: `POST /Library/VirtualFolders/Name?name=&newName=` with NO refreshLibrary parameter, i.e. refreshLibrary=false. WHAT UPSTREAM DOES WITH THAT REQUEST: LibraryStructureController.RenameVirtualFolder (v10.11.8 and master byte-identical apart from three added ClearIgnoreRuleCache() calls, plus a [RegularExpression] master added to a DIFFERENT action's name) moves the directory and then, in its finally block, `if (refreshLibrary) { ValidateTopLibraryFolders(ct, true); ... } else { await Task.Delay(1000); _libraryMonitor.Start(); }`. So on refreshLibrary=false Jellyfin deliberately validates nothing and keeps the CollectionFolder row under the OLD name, pointing at a directory that no longer exists, and serves it from /UserViews until some later scan. THE ASSERTION: the journey asserts the ROOT VIEW converges — after the rename no CollectionFolder still carries the old name, the new name is materialized, and the root's CollectionFolder count is unchanged end to end — over /Items + /UserViews. It used to assert only that /Library/VirtualFolders lists the new name, which upstream builds by walking the user-views DIRECTORY (LibraryManager.GetVirtualFolders, LibraryManager.cs:1527-1572, identical in both trees: it matches each directory against GetUserRootFolder().Children by path and leaves ItemId NULL when nothing matches), so it is the one surface a stale DB row cannot corrupt — and both servers passed it while only one was right. WHY FERROFIN MUST NOT COPY IT: Ferrofin derives a CollectionFolder's id from its directory path and get_virtual_folders mints a row for every directory it sees, so leaving the vacated row behind yields TWO rows where upstream has one stale one — measured before the fix as a permanent phantom library ('Movies (synth) Renamed', 5730b9eb5c86a66014cedd6ea527295f) that survived restarts and POST /Library/Refresh and showed up in the client sidebar. FerrofinVirtualFolderManager::rename_virtual_folder now deletes the row the vacated directory backed and runs prune_orphan_collection_folders (the port of ValidateTopLibraryFolders' remove leg — 'If the user has somehow deleted the collection directory, remove the metadata from the database', LibraryManager.cs:1172-1190, identical in both trees — also called from remove_virtual_folder and at LibraryScanner::scan start). CONSEQUENCE, flagged for the owner: the API handler rescans the renamed library UNCONDITIONALLY, not only when refreshLibrary is set, because deleting the old row cascades its children away (FK_BaseItems_BaseItems_ParentId ON DELETE CASCADE) and skipping the refresh would leave the renamed library empty; upstream can skip it only because it keeps the stale row and its children. The rescan is scoped to the renamed library when library_id_by_name resolves its id, which is the normal case (get_virtual_folders mints the row before the lookup); if it does not resolve, the fallback is a FULL library scan — more than upstream queues for this request — and that arm now logs at WARN so an unrequested full pass is attributable. Dashboard-only op. (b) THE OWNER QUESTION, not to be resolved by an agent. All five of Jellyfin's plugins are bundled in-assembly, so `PluginManager.CreatePluginInstance` builds `new LocalPlugin(instance.AssemblyFilePath, ...)` (v10.11.8 PluginManager.cs:541,559) and `Path` is a .dll FILE. `ChangePluginState` (:513) flips `Manifest.Status` in memory FIRST, then `SaveManifest` (:364) does `File.WriteAllText(Path.Combine(path, "meta.json"))` and catches only `ArgumentException`, so the `DirectoryNotFoundException` escapes the action and `ExceptionMiddleware` maps it to 404 (`DirectoryNotFoundException => Status404NotFound`, identical v10.11.8/master). Confirmed in the container log: "Error processing request: Could not find a part of the path '/jellyfin/MediaBrowser.Providers.dll/meta.json'. URL POST /Plugins/.../Disable". Net effect on Jellyfin: a 204 never changes state and a state change is always reported 404. `git diff v10.11.8 master -- PluginManager.cs` is ONE hunk (line 567, ImageResourceName) — master does not fix it. (b) THE OWNER QUESTION, not to be resolved by an agent. Jellyfin's toggle takes effect at the NEXT BOOT: `EnablePlugin`/`DisablePlugin` call `ProcessAlternative`, whose last two lines are `plugin.Manifest.Status = PluginStatus.Restart; plugin.Manifest.AutoUpdate = false;` (:882, commented "This value is memory only - so that the web will show restart required"). Ferrofin's toggle takes effect IMMEDIATELY — every consumer asks the PluginManager at use time (ferrofin-extensions file_transformation.rs:244,313,333; merge_versions.rs:179,212,246; ferrofin-wasm/src/lib.rs:558-575 behind a TTL cache), never only at boot — so it reports Active/Disabled and reporting `Restart` would be a false statement about Ferrofin's own behaviour. Both values are schema-valid (`PluginStatus` in the vendored contract is [Active,Restart,Deleted,Superseded,Superceded,Malfunctioned,NotSupported,Disabled]), and jellyfin-web computes `isEnabled = Status !== 'Disabled'`, so Jellyfin's own value leaves the dashboard toggle reading ENABLED right after a disable. The question: do we (i) keep immediate-effect + truthful Active/Disabled [today], (ii) keep immediate-effect but ALSO emit Restart for jellyfin-web's restart banner, or (iii) port Jellyfin's defer-until-restart semantics? If (ii)/(iii): crates/ferrofin-api/src/handlers/plugins.rs `to_plugin_info`/`to_plugin_manifest` plus a toggled-since-boot set in ferrofin-core/src/plugin_manager.rs `set_enabled`; no query/repository/DTO path is involved. Neither probe issues one. Do not add an "idempotent toggle" fact. The mutate/restore pair is wrapped in try/finally (reviewer-fix pass) and restores through `restore_plugin_state`, which READS the status first and issues nothing when it already matches — so an interrupted or timed-out run cannot leave a Jellyfin plugin Disabled for the rest of the container's life, and the restore itself can never become the no-op toggle it exists to avoid. Verified after the change: one full Active→Disabled→Active cycle per route per server, all 5 Jellyfin plugins and the 1 Ferrofin plugin back at `Active`, none at `Restart`.
